Initial alert on j.martinez was a red herring. arguments.summary: Ransomware execution detected on endpoint 10.0.6.30 (WS-IT-101). The attack originated from compromised host 10.0.5.14 (WS-FIN-042), which exhibited Cobalt Strike beaconing behavior. Initial access likely occurred via phishing or exploit, leading to lateral movement and eventual ransomware deployment. The crypt0r.exe payload encrypted user documents and deleted Volume Shadow Copies. Despite EDR visibility, the malicious process was not initially flagged. Firewall successfully blocked the source IP post-detection. A sandbox analysis incorrectly classified the payload as clean, indicating evasion capabilities.

arguments.summary: Ransomware execution detected on endpoint 10.0.6.30 (WS-IT-101). Initial access traced to source IP 10.0.5.14, which had prior indicators of compromise including Cobalt Strike beaconing. arguments.summary: A data exfiltration incident was detected originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), attributed to user CORP\jsmith in the Finance department. The threat actor used Cobalt Strike beaconing (ET TROJAN signature) to establish C2 communication with 10.0.5.14 and exfiltrated over 2.3 GB of sensitive data via DNS tunneling to c2.evil-example.com. Initial access likely occurred via a malicious payload, though the initial vector remains unconfirmed. The compromised host was used for lateral movement via SMB to 10.0.3.10. Response actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall, resetting the user's credentials and MFA, executing a post-breach hardening playbook, and detecting a related Linux dropper on the endpoint. The sandbox incorrectly classified the payload as clean.

arguments.summary: A critical data exfiltration incident was detected involving DNS tunneling from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) to external C2 domain c2.evil-example.com. The exfiltration, originating from the Finance department, involved over 2.3 GB of sensitive data containing PII and financial records. Initial access was likely achieved via a malicious payload triggering a Cobalt Strike beacon. Lateral movement via SMB was observed, and data was exfiltrated using high-volume DNS TXT queries. The threat was contained by isolating the infected host and blocking the C2 IP. No evidence of ransomware deployment or domain-wide compromise was found.

timeline.description: Initial outbound connection to 198.51.100.23 (C2 IP) from WS-FIN-042.
Suspicious rundll32 execution detected from Temp directory on WS-FIN-042.
IDS alert triggered: 'ET TROJAN Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 Activity' from WS-FIN-042.
Lateral movement detected: SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to file server 10.0.5.50.
DLP alert triggered: Large-scale data exfiltration via DNS tunneling (TXT queries to c2.evil-example.com) from 10.0.7.50 to 10.0.5.14.
Containment: C2 IP 10.0.5.14 blocked at firewall; host WS-FIN-042 isolated from network.
Eradication: Endpoint scanned and cleaned; user jsmith's credentials reset; security policies hardened.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious rundll32 Execution from Temp Directory
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\\rundll32.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 
      - '%TEMP%'
      - '/c'
      - 'powershell'
  condition: selection
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/011/
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software updates
  - Admin scripts (rare)
author: SOC Team

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious rundll32 Execution from Temp Directory
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\\rundll32.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 
      - '%TEMP%'
      - '/c'
      - 'powershell'
  condition: selection
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/011/
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software updates
  - Admin scripts (rare)
author: SOC Team

title: Outbound Cobalt Strike Beacon to External IP
detection:
  network_connection:
    DestinationIP: '*.*.*.*'
    DestinationPort: 443
    Protocol: tcp
    BytesSent: < 1000
    BytesReceived: > 10000
    Frequency: 'every 60s over 5m'
  process_indicator:
    Image: '*\\rundll32.exe, *\\powershell.exe'
  condition: network_connection and process_indicator
level: critical
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate API polling (unlikely due to process context)
author: SOC Team

Host WS-FIN-042 in Finance department is compromised and serving as an access point for potential data exfiltration and network propagation. Despite detection, containment actions were blocked due to consensus failure in Admin phase.

timeline.description: Initial outbound HTTPS connection from WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) to known-bad IP 198.51.100.23 on port 443.
Suspicious rundll32.exe execution detected from Temp directory on WS-FIN-042.
IDS alerts on Cobalt Strike beaconing (ET TROJAN signature) from WS-FIN-042 to C2 server.
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042, indicating potential credential misuse or brute-force attempt.
Successful SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to file server 10.0.5.50, confirming lateral movement.
Port scan detected from WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) to IT workstation 10.0.4.1, triggering initial alert.
EDR/NDR confirms persistent C2 beaconing, encoded PowerShell, and unsigned DLL loading on WS-FIN-042.
SIEM correlation identifies 847 beaconing events over past 7 days, confirming long-term compromise.
Containment actions (firewall block, account disable, endpoint isolation) rejected due to consensus failure in Admin phase.

arguments.summary: Suspicious authentication event from IP 10.0.5.14 to domain controller 10.0.8.200 triggered initial alert. Investigation revealed that host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), owned by user jsmith, was compromised via a phishing email leading to Cobalt Strike beaconing. The attacker performed credential theft, attempted Kerberos pre-authentication attacks, and initiated lateral movement via SMB. The compromised host was isolated via firewall block and the user's credentials were reset. UEBA did not flag high risk due to low anomaly score, indicating evasion of behavioral baselines.

arguments.summary: Suspicious authentication from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) led to detection of Cobalt Strike beaconing activity. The host, owned by user jsmith in Finance, was compromised via phishing (evidenced by encoded PowerShell from Outlook). Adversary attempted Kerberos pre-auth brute-force against user j.martinez, succeeded in authentication, and performed lateral movement via SMB. Actions taken include full host scan, credential reset for jsmith, and session revocation for j.martinez. UEBA initially flagged low risk due to normal business hour activity, indicating detection gap.

timeline.description: Initial outbound HTTPS connection from WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) to known malicious IP 198.51.100.23
Suspicious rundll32.exe execution from Temp directory on WS-FIN-042
IDS alert: Cobalt Strike beaconing detected (ET TROJAN signature)
Failed Kerberos pre-authentication (Event ID 4771) for user j.martinez from WS-FIN-042
Lateral movement via SMB to file server 10.0.5.50 from WS-FIN-042
Alert generated for suspicious authentication pattern involving j.martinez and source 10.0.5.14 (misreported; actual source was 10.0.5.42)
EPP full scan initiated on WS-FIN-042; detected Linux dropper in cron directory
Credentials for user jsmith reset; MFA token re-enrollment initiated
All active sessions and API keys for j.martinez revoked

  success_event:

  condition: fail_event and success_event
  timeframe: 5m
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/003/

    meta:

        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"

    condition:

}

arguments.summary: Initial low-severity port scan alert from 10.0.5.14 escalated following correlation with historical IDS alerts and EDR telemetry. Investigation revealed that the true source of malicious activity was host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), a high-criticality finance workstation exhibiting Cobalt Strike beaconing, suspicious PowerShell execution, and lateral movement via SMB. The original scanner (10.0.4.1) was benign; the compromised host had initiated C2 communications and internal reconnaissance. Immediate containment actions were executed on WS-FIN-042.

Successful SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to file server 10.0.5.50, confirming lateral movement
Port scan alert from 10.0.5.14 to 10.0.4.1 triggers investigation
Correlation identifies WS-FIN-042 as origin of C2 traffic and malicious activity
Containment actions initiated: WS-FIN-042 isolated, user credentials revoked

arguments.summary: A low-severity port scan alert from 10.0.5.14 (WS-FIN-042) escalated into a confirmed compromise involving Cobalt Strike beaconing, lateral movement, and exploitation of CVE-2024-3094. The initial vector was a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell download from Outlook, leading to DLL sideloading via rundll32. Despite detection, response actions (firewall block, IAM lockout, Ansible remediation) were blocked due to consensus policy failures.
